finding: The only open table found with explicit absolute-power units is the Muse headband study by Hashemi et al.: the regression intercepts in Table 2 are log10 total band power in µV² for males aged 42 during an eyes-closed 1-minute category-naming calibration (CAL), at two frontal (AF7, AF8) and two temporoparietal (TP9, TP10) dry electrodes referenced to Fpz. The values are far below conventional wet-cap values because of the Fpz reference next to the frontal sites, the 2 to 36 Hz band-pass (which guts the 0 to 2 Hz 'delta' band) and dry consumer electrodes.
baseline: Absolute values (no baseline): model intercept = estimate for males at the mean age of 42 years; both conditions eyes closed (CAL task, NFB meditation).
subjects: 6029 Muse users aged 18-88 (4379 male, 1650 female), uncontrolled home or app environment; first five clean sessions averaged per user.
electrodes_band_window: Muse: AF7, AF8, TP9, TP10 referenced to Fpz, 220 Hz sampling, 2-36 Hz band-pass, 50/60 Hz notch; FFT at 1 Hz resolution over the whole cleaned session (CAL 1 min; NFB 3-20 min); total power per band summed over 0-2, 3-7, 8-13, 14-30 Hz then log10-transformed; 1.16 s epochs exceeding 275 µV² rejected.

source.authors: Hashemi A, Pino LJ, Moffat G, Mathewson KJ, Aimone C, Bennett PJ, Schmidt LA, Sekuler AB
source.title: Characterizing Population EEG Dynamics throughout Adulthood

evidence_location: Materials and Methods, 'EEG recording and processing' and 'EEG measures' (units, bands, filter); Results, Tables 2 (CAL) and 3 (NFB), 'Intercept' column; text before Table 2 defines the intercept as the estimate for males at 42 years.
quote: Total power (µV2) was calculated for the δ (0–2 Hz), θ (3–7 Hz), α (8–13 Hz), and β (14–30 Hz)
caveats: Explicit units but not a standard montage: dry electrodes, Fpz reference (frontal channels nearly short-circuited to the reference), 2-36 Hz filter makes the 0-2 Hz 'delta' value physically meaningless, sessions include a mental task and meditation rather than quiet rest, and no eyes-open condition. Whether 'total power' is a sum over 1 Hz bins (per band) is implied by the wording but not demonstrated. Use only as an order-of-magnitude anchor for a consumer headband, not for a 10-20 cap.

finding: No open, standard-montage table of absolute resting band power (µV²) or amplitude (µV) at frontal, central and parietal/occipital sites in healthy adults with unambiguous units was found within the budget; the classic sources are closed or report statistics, log values of unstated base, or maps only.
numbers: Not found. Closest misses: Enoch et al. 2008 (PLoS One 3:e3620, open) Table 4 gives 'Alpha EEG power (µv2) at PZ' as 4.25 (0.4) to 4.51 (0.3) by genotype, but the text says these are log-transformed with the base not stated; Fröhlich et al. 2021 (Front Aging Neurosci 13:675689, open) shows 'mean absolute power in µV2' only as brain maps (figure) for 80+-year-olds; Lee et al. 2017 (J Behav Addict 6:387-398, open) reports 'Absolute power (µV2)' statistics but no site means; Bosch-Bayard et al. 2020 (Front Neuroinform 14:33, open) provides normative z-scores of log source spectra, no scalp µV² values.

source.authors: Barry RJ, Clarke AR, Johnstone SJ, Magee CA, Rushby JA
source.title: EEG differences between eyes-closed and eyes-open resting conditions

evidence_location: Barry et al. 2007 abstract only (Europe PMC); full text closed. Gasser et al. 1988 (Electroencephalogr Clin Neurophysiol 69(2):91-99, DOI 10.1016/0013-4694(88)90204-0) and Chen et al. 2008 (NeuroImage 41(2):561-574) are closed; Kan et al. 2017 (Neurophysiology, DOI 10.1007/s11062-018-9706-6) is paywalled on Springer (only the reference list was served).
quote: Fourier transformed to provide estimates for absolute power in the delta, theta, alpha and beta bands
caveats: Tried: Europe PMC full-text searches for open papers containing eyes-closed/eyes-open, 'absolute power' and µV² with O1/Fz/Cz; Hinrichs et al. 2020 (Sci Rep 10:5218) has no band values; Trammell et al. 2017 (Front Aging Neurosci 9:364) tabulates only model coefficients; Rodríguez-Martínez et al. 2012 (BMC Neurosci 13:104) tabulates only alpha peak frequency; Danker-Hopfe et al. 2019 and van der Meer et al. 2023 give no absolute tables; the NCBI Bookshelf textbook (Britton et al. 2016) and PMC pages were blocked by reCAPTCHA. The LEMON dataset paper (Babayan et al. 2019) was not opened because no paper reporting its band powers with units was found in search. A normative table with explicit µV² units will probably require a closed source (Barry 2007 Table 1; Gasser 1988) or a direct computation from an open dataset such as LEMON.

finding: The 2017 IFCN-endorsed clinical glossary states that the adult alpha rhythm (8-13 Hz, posterior, eyes closed) has an amplitude that varies but is mostly below 50 µV, and is often much higher in children.
numbers: Alpha rhythm: 'mostly below 50 µV in the adult'; frequency 8-13 Hz inclusive; maximal over the occipital areas; best seen with the eyes closed; blocked or attenuated by attention and mental effort.
baseline: Absolute amplitude as read by clinical electroencephalographers (peak-to-peak by convention, see the glossary's 'Amplitude, EEG' entry); no reference condition.
subjects: Consensus glossary (no sample); applies to adults.
electrodes_band_window: Posterior/occipital scalp derivations, 8-13 Hz; visual reading of routine EEG, no fixed window.

source.authors: Kane N, Acharya J, Benickzy S, Caboclo L, Finnigan S, Kaplan PW, Shibasaki H, Pressler R, van Putten MJAM
source.title: A revised glossary of terms most commonly used by clinical electroencephalographers and updated proposal for the report format of the EEG findings. Revision 2017

evidence_location: Glossary entry 'Alpha rhythm' (section 2, alphabetical list); the entry 'Amplitude, EEG' defines amplitude as usually peak-to-peak in µV.
quote: Amplitude varies but is mostly below 50 µV in the adult, but often much higher in children.
caveats: A visual-reading convention (peak-to-peak on a bipolar or referential montage), not a measured mean; it gives an upper bound rather than a typical value. The glossary gives no lower bound and no RMS value.

finding: The same glossary puts fronto-central beta rhythm (14-30 Hz, wakefulness) mostly below 30 µV.
numbers: Beta rhythm: 14-30 Hz (wave duration 33-72 ms); 'Amplitude of fronto-central beta rhythm varies but is mostly below 30 µV'.
baseline: Absolute amplitude (peak-to-peak convention), no reference condition.

source.authors: Kane N, Acharya J, Benickzy S, Caboclo L, Finnigan S, Kaplan PW, Shibasaki H, Pressler R, van Putten MJAM
source.title: A revised glossary of terms most commonly used by clinical electroencephalographers and updated proposal for the report format of the EEG findings. Revision 2017

quote: Amplitude of fronto-central beta rhythm varies but is mostly below 30 µV.
caveats: Upper bound by convention; other beta rhythms (diffuse or drug-induced, e.g. benzodiazepines, intravenous anaesthetics) are noted but not quantified.

finding: The glossary gives the mu rhythm (7-11 Hz arch-shaped waves over central or centro-parietal regions) an amplitude mostly below 50 µV, blocked by contralateral movement, thought of movement, readiness to move or tactile stimulation.
numbers: Mu rhythm: 7-11 Hz; 'Amplitude varies but is mostly below 50 µV'.
electrodes_band_window: Central or centro-parietal scalp, 7-11 Hz, visual reading.

source.authors: Kane N, Acharya J, Benickzy S, Caboclo L, Finnigan S, Kaplan PW, Shibasaki H, Pressler R, van Putten MJAM
source.title: A revised glossary of terms most commonly used by clinical electroencephalographers and updated proposal for the report format of the EEG findings. Revision 2017

quote: Amplitude varies but is mostly below 50 µV. Blocked or attenuated most clearly by contralateral movement, thought of movement
caveats: Same bound as alpha; in practice mu is usually smaller and visible in only a fraction of adults, but the glossary does not quantify that.

finding: For sleep, the glossary's 'Deep sleep' entry carries the scoring criterion for slow waves: stage N3 is dominated (at least 20 percent) by delta waves of 0.5-2 Hz with peak-to-peak amplitude above 75 µV measured over the frontal regions. Waking delta is not given an amplitude; the related 'Low voltage EEG' entry (a normal waking variant) is defined as activity not greater than 20 µV over all head regions.
numbers: Deep sleep (N3): delta waves 0.5-2 Hz, peak-to-peak amplitude >75 µV, frontal regions, occupying >=20 percent of the epoch; Low voltage EEG: amplitude not greater than 20 µV over all head regions, composed mainly of beta, theta and some delta.
subjects: Consensus glossary (criterion originates from the AASM sleep-scoring rules it cites: Iber et al. 2007, Silber et al. 2007).
electrodes_band_window: Frontal derivations, 0.5-2 Hz, scored per epoch (30 s epochs in AASM practice, not stated in the glossary).

source.authors: Kane N, Acharya J, Benickzy S, Caboclo L, Finnigan S, Kaplan PW, Shibasaki H, Pressler R, van Putten MJAM
source.title: A revised glossary of terms most commonly used by clinical electroencephalographers and updated proposal for the report format of the EEG findings. Revision 2017

evidence_location: Glossary entries 'Deep sleep' and 'Low voltage EEG'.
quote: slow delta waves of frequency 0.5 to 2 Hz and peak-to-peak amplitude >75 µV, measured over the frontal regions
caveats: The 75 µV figure is a scoring threshold, not a typical amplitude; the primary rule is in the AASM manual (closed) and Silber MH et al. 2007, J Clin Sleep Med 3(2):121-131 (DOI 10.5664/jcsm.26814), which was not opened here. The glossary gives no amplitude for waking delta or for frontal midline theta.

finding: Propofol general anaesthesia: the open review by Purdon and colleagues states that the anaesthetic signatures (frontal alpha and slow oscillations) are 5 to 20 times larger in amplitude than the awake EEG; no µV value for the propofol frontal alpha itself is printed.
numbers: Factor of 5 to 20 (anaesthetized-state EEG amplitudes versus the awake state, Fig. 2 legend; slow-oscillation amplitudes 5 to 20 times the awake gamma/beta amplitudes, text); burst-suppression threshold ±5 microvolts (Fig. 8 legend).
baseline: Relative to the same subject's awake EEG (recordings in Fig. 2 are all from one subject).
subjects: Review; the factor is illustrated with recordings from a single subject.
electrodes_band_window: Frontal EEG (as used in operating-room monitors); slow oscillation 0.1-1 Hz, alpha 8-12 Hz; spectrogram-based description.

source.authors: Purdon PL, Sampson A, Pavone KJ, Brown EN
source.title: Clinical Electroencephalography for Anesthesiologists: Part I: Background and Basic Signatures

evidence_location: Fig. 2 legend (factor of 5 to 20 for anaesthetized states versus awake); section on propofol induction ('slow-oscillation amplitudes can be 5 to 20 times larger'); Fig. 8 legend (±5 microvolt burst-suppression threshold).
quote: slow-oscillation amplitudes can be 5 to 20 times larger than the amplitudes of the gamma and beta oscillations
caveats: Author manuscript read from PMC before the site started serving reCAPTCHA; the factor is a narrative statement without a sample. The quantitative primary (Purdon PL et al. 2013, PNAS 110(12):E1142-E1151, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1221180110, frontal alpha power in dB) could not be retrieved (PNAS and PMC blocked). Feshchenko VA, Veselis RA, Reinsel RA 2004 (Neuropsychobiology 50:257-266) says only that propofol rhythms 'exceed the baseline alpha-rhythm in power' (abstract).

finding: Frontal midline theta amplitude at Fz during tasks: not found in an open source. Kane et al. 2017 define 'Fronto-central theta' (synonym frontal midline theta, Ciganek rhythm) as a normal variant in the midline just anterior to the vertex during psychological stress and cognitive tasks, predominantly in young adults under 30, but give no amplitude.
numbers: None found. Kane 2017: theta rhythm 4 to <8 Hz; Fm theta appears 'predominantly in young healthy adults (<30 years of age)'.
electrodes_band_window: Midline frontal (Fz/FCz), theta 4-8 Hz (6-7 Hz typical per Inanaga 1998 abstract).

source.authors: Kane N, Acharya J, Benickzy S, Caboclo L, Finnigan S, Kaplan PW, Shibasaki H, Pressler R, van Putten MJAM
source.title: A revised glossary of terms most commonly used by clinical electroencephalographers and updated proposal for the report format of the EEG findings. Revision 2017

quote: Theta rhythm located in the midline, just anterior to the vertex, that occurs during psychological stress and cognitive tasks
caveats: Tried: abstracts of Takahashi N et al. 1997 (Clin Electroencephalogr 28:49-54) and Inanaga K 1998 (Psychiatry Clin Neurosci 52:555-566), full texts of Ishii R et al. 2014 (Front Hum Neurosci 8:406, MEG) and Onton J et al. 2005 (NeuroImage 27:341-356): none prints a µV amplitude. Niedermeyer's textbook (closed) was not checked. Mark as not found.

finding: In 268 middle-aged and older adults at rest (eyes open and closed pooled), the FOOOF aperiodic fit from 2 to 40 Hz at a frontal F3/Fz/F4 composite gave a mean exponent of 1.23 (SD 0.26) and a mean offset of 0.43 (SD 0.44); the exponent falls with age (r = -0.24).
numbers: Fronto-central aperiodic exponent 1.23 (SD 0.26); fronto-central aperiodic offset 0.43 (SD 0.44); age correlation with exponent r = -0.24 [95% CI -0.35, -0.13]; fronto-central individual alpha peak 9.31 Hz (SD 0.98); canonical theta-beta ratio 1.09 (0.68).
baseline: Absolute parameters (no baseline); offset is the FOOOF y-intercept in log10 power at 1 Hz; the units of the input power spectral density are not printed (average reference, 2 s Hamming windows).
subjects: 268 adults aged 36-84 (mean 55.8, SD 11.0; 146 female) from the MIDUS study (sub-samples Main, Twin, Milwaukee) with usable EEG.
electrodes_band_window: F3, Fz, F4 composite (average reference, Cz online reference imputed); FOOOF 1.0.0 fit over 2-40 Hz; six 1-minute resting periods (three eyes open, three eyes closed) epoched into 2 s segments with 50 percent overlap; values collapsed across eye conditions.

source.authors: Finley AJ, Angus DJ, van Reekum CM, Davidson RJ, Schaefer SM
source.title: Periodic and aperiodic contributions to theta-beta ratios across adulthood

evidence_location: Table 3 'Correlations and descriptive statistics between age and EEG metrics, collapsed across eyes open and eyes closed (n = 268)', rows 6 and 7 (Mean (SD) column); Methods section 2.5 for the 2-40 Hz FOOOF range and 2 s epochs; Table 2 for the sample.
quote: to fit aperiodic and periodic components from 2 to 40 Hz
caveats: Frontal sites only and an older sample (36-84); the offset's physical unit depends on the PSD scaling, which the paper does not state (0.43 log10 units would be about 2.7 µV²/Hz at 1 Hz only if the PSD was in µV²/Hz). The PMC version is the accepted text; a 2024 corrigendum (Psychophysiology 61:e14555) exists and was not read.

finding: In 46 adults resting with eyes open inside an MRI scanner (simultaneous EEG-fMRI, 32 channels), FOOOF fits over 1-50 Hz gave an average aperiodic exponent of 1.49 (SD 0.17, range 1.18-1.91) and an average offset of 5.19 (SD 0.36, range 4.36-6.29) 'log µV²'; residual alpha peak power averaged 0.85 log µV² (range 0.44-1.39), beta 0.46, gamma 0.32.
numbers: Offset 5.19 ± 0.36 (log μV2, range 4.36–6.29); exponent 1.49 ± 0.17 (range 1.18–1.91); offset-exponent correlation r = 0.92 ± 0.02; residual alpha 0.85 ± 0.20 log μV2, beta 0.46 ± 0.13, gamma 0.32 ± 0.07; mean FOOOF R² 0.64 (range 0.51-0.74).
baseline: Absolute parameters averaged over all subjects and channels; eyes-open rest.
subjects: 46 healthy adults, age 38.3 (SD 15.1, range 18-69), 9 women and 37 men.
electrodes_band_window: 32 channels (FCz online reference, re-referenced to average), 5 kHz sampling downsampled to 250 Hz after MRI-artifact removal; FFT with 2 s Hanning windows, 0.5 Hz resolution; FOOOF 1-50 Hz, fixed (no knee) mode; spectra per fMRI TR interval.

source.authors: Jacob MS, Roach BJ, Sargent KS, Mathalon DH, Ford JM
source.title: Aperiodic measures of neural excitability are associated with anticorrelated hemodynamic networks at rest: A combined EEG-fMRI study

evidence_location: Results, first paragraph of section 3.1 ('Aperiodic and periodic EEG components'), referring to Fig. 2A-C; Methods 2.6 for FFT and FOOOF settings; Table 1 for the sample.
quote: The average spectral offset across all subjects and channels was 5.19±0.36 (log μV2, range 4.36–6.29)
caveats: An offset of 5.19 log10 units at 1 Hz (about 150,000 µV²) is incompatible with a µV²/Hz density, so the FFT scaling is not per hertz: treat the printed offset as scaling-dependent and use only the exponent and the alpha-to-background difference. EEG recorded inside a 3 T scanner after gradient and ballistocardiogram artifact correction; the authors' own abstract flags the scanner setting. Not a normal eyes-closed quiet-rest condition.

finding: The reference paper for the method (Donoghue et al. 2020) could not be opened here (Nature page and the PMC author manuscript blocked; Europe PMC returns errors for that manuscript), and its 2018 bioRxiv version (v1) contains only an illustrative fit, so its scalp exponent values are unverified. Two large resting studies that fit the aperiodic component (Merkin et al. 2023, 85 younger and 92 older adults, eyes closed, 2-40 Hz; Cesnaite et al. 2023, 1703 adults aged about 70, eyes closed, 2-40 Hz) report group differences and correlations but print no mean offsets or exponents in their text.
numbers: Donoghue 2018 preprint (bioRxiv 299859v1), Fig. 3 legend example only: 'broadband offset = −21.4 au; slope = −1.12 au/Hz' (illustrative, dataset not identified). Merkin 2023: older adults had a lower global offset (Z = -5.84, r = -0.44) and smaller exponent (Z = -5.34, r = -0.40), no means printed. Cesnaite 2023: 1/f slope negatively associated with age, no means printed.
subjects: Merkin: 85 younger (22.2 ± 3.9 y) and 92 older (66.1 ± 8.2 y) adults; Cesnaite: 1703 adults (mean 70, SD 4.7).
electrodes_band_window: Merkin: 57 or 62 electrodes, average reference, 3 min eyes closed, Welch 2 s windows, FOOOF 2-40 Hz; Cesnaite: 31 channels, 20 min eyes closed, aperiodic fit 2-40 Hz.

source.authors: Donoghue T, Haller M, Peterson EJ, Varma P, Sebastian P, Gao R, Noto T, Lara AH, Wallis JD, Knight RT, Shestyuk A, Voytek B
source.title: Parameterizing neural power spectra into periodic and aperiodic components

evidence_location: Not accessible (abstract only via Europe PMC, PMID 33230329, PMC8106550). Merkin A et al. 2023, Neurobiology of Aging 121:78-87, DOI 10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2022.09.003, read as bioRxiv 2021.08.31.458328 (Results and Methods). Cesnaite E et al. 2023, NeuroImage 268:119810, DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119810, read as bioRxiv 2021.08.26.457768.
caveats: The widely quoted 'exponent about 1 to 2 at the scalp' could not be tied to a verifiable sentence in Donoghue 2020 here; the Finley 2022 and Jacob 2021 entries above are the verifiable scalp values found (1.23 and 1.49). A closed-source check of Donoghue 2020 Fig. 5 (EEG across age) is still needed if the site wants to cite it.

finding: In 40 healthy older controls, occipital alpha power (relative power around the individual alpha peak, O1/Oz/O2) averaged 49.1 with eyes closed and 18.9 with eyes open, an alpha reactivity (EC minus EO over EC) of 0.56; the printed means imply the eyes-closed value is about two and a half times the eyes-open value (my division, not printed).
numbers: Healthy controls: eyes-closed alpha power 49.1 [95% CI 41.9, 56.3]; eyes-open alpha power 18.9 [16.1, 21.7]; alpha reactivity 0.56 [0.50, 0.63]; individual alpha peak 8.8 Hz [8.4, 9.2]. (AD: 34.4 / 24.2 / 0.24; Lewy body dementia: 39.7 / 36.7 / 0.08.)
baseline: Eyes-closed rest versus eyes-open rest, same participants; alpha power expressed as relative power within the individual alpha peak ± 2 Hz (units of the relative measure not printed; the values suggest percent of total power).
subjects: 40 healthy controls, mean age 73.4 (SD 6.6), 25 men and 15 women (plus 21 Alzheimer's disease and 41 Lewy body dementia patients).
electrodes_band_window: O1, Oz, O2 (128-channel cap, average reference after preprocessing, 0.3-54 Hz); 150 s eyes closed and 150 s eyes open; first 45 artefact-free 2 s epochs per condition; Bartlett PSD at 0.25 Hz; band = individual alpha peak frequency ± 2 Hz.

source.authors: Schumacher J, Thomas AJ, Peraza LR, Firbank M, Cromarty R, Hamilton CA, Donaghy PC, O'Brien JT, Taylor JP
source.title: EEG alpha reactivity and cholinergic system integrity in Lewy body dementia and Alzheimer's disease

evidence_location: Table 2 'Group comparison of EEG characteristics and NBM volume' (mean [95% confidence interval]; footnote: estimated from O1, Oz, O2 using individual alpha peak frequencies); Methods, 'Alpha reactivity analysis' (formula and definition of alpha power as relative power).
quote: alpha power was computed as the relative power within a frequency bin around the individual alpha peak frequency
caveats: Older adults (about 73 years), not young adults, and relative rather than absolute power, so the ratio of relative values understates the absolute-power ratio if total power also changes with eye closure. Frontal sites not reported. Best open source with explicit EC and EO values found; the classic young-adult table (Barry 2007) is closed.

finding: The classic eyes-closed versus eyes-open study (28 university students, 9 scalp regions) reports, in its abstract, reductions in across-scalp mean absolute delta, theta, alpha and beta power from eyes closed to eyes open, with topographic changes in every band except alpha: reduced lateral-frontal delta and posterior theta, and decreased posterior but increased frontal beta with the eyes open. The table values are behind a paywall.
numbers: Directions only (abstract): delta, theta, alpha, beta all lower with eyes open; alpha reduction without topographic change; beta decreases posteriorly and increases frontally; delta decreases at lateral frontal sites; theta decreases posteriorly; skin conductance rises from EC to EO.
baseline: Eyes-closed rest versus eyes-open rest, within subjects.
electrodes_band_window: 9 scalp regions (electrode set not in abstract); FFT absolute power in delta, theta, alpha and beta bands; window not in abstract.

source.authors: Barry RJ, Clarke AR, Johnstone SJ, Magee CA, Rushby JA
source.title: EEG differences between eyes-closed and eyes-open resting conditions

evidence_location: Abstract (Results paragraph), via Europe PMC; full text closed.
quote: Reductions were found in across-scalp mean absolute delta, theta, alpha and beta from the eyes-closed to eyes-open condition.
caveats: No magnitudes available without the full text; no open paper quoting its table values was found. Companion abstract: Chen AC, Feng W, Zhao H, Yin Y, Wang P 2008, NeuroImage 41(2):561-574 (DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2007.12.064; 15 healthy college women, 128 channels, 3 min each condition) reports prefrontal delta field power enhanced from EC to EO (t = -2.72, p < 0.02) while theta (t = 4.04), alpha-1 and alpha-2 (t = 4.12) and beta-1 (t = 4.42) field powers were reduced; also abstract only.

finding: Wan et al. (open) define EC-to-EO alpha reactivity as (EC alpha power minus EO alpha power) divided by EC alpha power at O1/O2/Oz in 21 young and 19 older adults, but the paper prints only correlations with fMRI and lesion measures; group-mean reactivity values appear only in scatter plots (Figures 2c, 4c, 5c-e), so no number can be quoted.
numbers: No group means printed. Alpha band 8-12 Hz; artifact threshold 75 μV; correlations r = -0.389 (young, p = .041) and r = -0.630 (older, p = .004) between reactivity and cholinergic connectivity change.
baseline: Eyes closed versus eyes open, within subjects (fraction of EC power lost on eye opening).
subjects: 21 young adults (EEG-fMRI) and 19 older adults aged 60-85 (EEG in a separate session).
electrodes_band_window: O1, O2, Oz averaged; periodogram over 1 s epochs; 8-12 Hz; 128-channel cap for older adults.

source.authors: Wan L, Huang H, Schwab N, Tanner J, Rajan A, Lam NB, Zaborszky L, Li CR, Price CC, Ding M
source.title: From eyes-closed to eyes-open: Role of cholinergic projections in EC-to-EO alpha reactivity revealed by combining EEG and MRI

evidence_location: Methods 2.4 'Power spectral analysis of EEG data' (definition); Results 3.1.3 and 3.2.3 (correlations); figures only for values.
quote: the larger the alpha reactivity, the more the EC‐to‐EO alpha power decrease from EC to EO
caveats: Useful for the definition of alpha reactivity and for the two age groups, not for a number. Note the volume/pages differ from the task sheet: Europe PMC lists Hum Brain Mapp 2019;40(2):566-577, DOI 10.1002/hbm.24395 (the citation line inside the PMC copy agrees). No open young-adult source with explicit EC and EO power values (or a frontal EC/EO ratio) was found; Hashemi 2016 has no eyes-open condition and Kan et al. 2017 is paywalled.
